clue.text: Finally, zookeepers nervously fed larger pride

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word zookeepers
nervously suggests jittery movement, so the letters of fed larger are jumbled

explanation.surface: A zookeeper anxiously feeds a big group of lions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' looks like a lion group belonging to the zoo scene, but it is the definition in its sense of self-esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride in the sense of vanity or self-esteem is a synonym of high regard for oneself.

clue.text: Son gets syrup drink

parts.note: cockney rhyming slang: syrup of figs means a wig

explanation.surface: A boy is given a sugary drink.
explanation.walkthrough: SYRUP is British rhyming slang for a wig (from 'syrup of figs'), so 'syrup' is not about sweet liquid at all.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a gulp or large mouthful of liquid is a drink.

clue.text: Head of facilities on the hunt?

parts.note: the facilities is a euphemism for the toilet, the loo
a king is the head of a country

explanation.surface: The manager of the facilities department is out searching for something.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Head of facilities' as a king of the toilet: LOO then KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone searching is said to be seeking, which is what on the hunt means.

clue.text: Film in attic?

definitions.meaning: the 1959 British film starring Laurence Harvey
an attic is the uppermost space in a house

explanation.surface: A film set in a loft.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1959 film title, and literally the chamber at the summit of a house, as an attic is.

clue.text: Dig melon out — get rich from this!

indicators.note: out signals the letters of dig melon are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone digs up a melon in hope of a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A source of great wealth, figuratively or a literal mine yielding the precious metal, makes one rich.

clue.text: Begrudge gift quietly set aside

indicators.note: set aside means the quiet letter is removed from the gift word

parts.note: a gift is a present
P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly puts away a present they are jealous of.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge is to feel bitter about something, a close synonym.

clue.text: Impressive stone Pict houses

indicators.note: houses means the words stone Pict contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: An ancient Pictish stone shelters dwellings and is grand.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand and heroic in scale, so impressive is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Soldiers also included in scheme

indicators.note: included in places the word for also within the word for scheme

parts.note: a scheme is a plan
also means too

explanation.surface: Troops are part of the plan as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of soldiers forming a subdivision of a company.

clue.text: Daughter in possession of coke truly suffering withdrawal symptoms

indicators.note: the daughter letter is held inside the scrambled letters, which possess it
suffering suggests something being knocked about, so the letters of coke truly are rearranged

explanation.surface: A daughter caught with cocaine is genuinely going through withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' scrambles COKE TRULY, and D goes inside, as 'in possession of' says.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the abrupt unpleasant effects of quitting a drug at once, i.e. its withdrawal.

clue.text: One might be painting destroyer?

parts.note: an icon is a religious painting, so a breaker of icons destroys paintings

explanation.surface: Someone who vandalises artworks.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual sense is one who attacks cherished beliefs; literally it is a smasher of religious images.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a breaker of holy images, which are religious pictures.

clue.text: Bitterness caused by broadcast of Asterix, perhaps

indicators.note: broadcast suggests something spoken over the air, so a word sounding the same is meant

parts.note: Asterix, the comic-book hero, is an example of a Gaul

explanation.surface: Someone resents how the Asterix cartoons are aired.
explanation.definitionFit: Bile, and figuratively rancour or resentment, so it means bitterness.

clue.text: Senate giving criminal something to take away?

indicators.note: criminal means the letters of senate giving are treated badly and rearranged

explanation.surface: The Senate gives a crook a takeaway meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take away' means subtract: the minus symbol tells you to take away.
explanation.definitionFit: The minus symbol instructs subtraction, i.e. something telling you to take away.

clue.text: Four in five answer test

indicators.note: in places the Roman four inside the other letters

parts.note: V is five in Roman numerals
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four out of five answers in an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral university examination, short for viva voce, is a test.

clue.text: Staff leave vegetables

parts.note: to staff is to man, as in crewing a post
to leave is to get out

explanation.surface: Employees go off with the greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' is a verb here: to man something.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow peas, eaten pod and all; the word serves as a plural for these vegetables.

clue.text: Type of grid that could make Christopher reportedly angry

indicators.note: reportedly means a word that is said like the short form of Christopher is meant

parts.note: Chris is the short form of Christopher
angry means cross

explanation.surface: A grid pattern that might enrage a man called Christopher.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern of intersecting lines is a type of grid, such as a lattice.

clue.text: Italian food: tackle a lot, then second helping of pizza!

parts.note: tackle, as fishing gear, is a rig
a ton means a lot

indicators.note: second helping means the second letter of the word pizza

explanation.surface: Tuck into lots of Italian food, then have another slice of pizza.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridged tubular pasta, which is an Italian food.

clue.text: Barman's shake Mr Bean regularly sent back

definitions.note: a composer, writing music in bars, is a bar man

parts.note: to wag is to shake, as a tail

indicators.note: sent back means those letters are read from right to left
regularly takes every other letter of Mr Bean

explanation.surface: A bartender makes a cocktail; Mr Bean is repeatedly turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman' is not a bartender but a composer, whose music is written in bars; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The German operatic composer, and composers write in bars, hence a whimsical man of bars.

clue.text: Reread if novel somewhat lacking in atmosphere?

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of reread if take a fresh order

explanation.surface: Rereading a novel that falls a bit flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' is not a book but the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin air at altitude is described this way: lower in oxygen, with less atmosphere.

clue.text: Fool that's got a good grip?

definitions.meaning: a fool is a dupe, someone easily taken in
a suction cup or an octopus's pad clings firmly

explanation.surface: A fool who holds on tight.
explanation.definitionFit: A gullible person, and also a suction device or organ that clings tightly.

clue.text: My face is friendly

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
a clock's face is its dial

explanation.surface: Someone notes that their face looks amiable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation, matched by COR, a British cry of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm and amiable, so friendly is a synonym.

clue.text: Harbour oddly deep and steep

parts.note: a marina is a harbour for boats

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of deep

explanation.surface: A harbour with odd, deep and sheer sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' looks like an adjective for the harbour but is the verb to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak food in a seasoned liquid is to steep it.

clue.text: Placate monkey eating small round things

indicators.note: eating means the monkey word swallows the other inside it

parts.note: an ape is a monkey in loose usage
peas are small round vegetables

explanation.surface: Soothe a monkey by letting it eat peas.
explanation.walkthrough: The monkey 'eating' its food is the container signal; strictly an ape is not a monkey, a liberty setters often take.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify or calm someone, a direct synonym of placate.

clue.text: Picture maker turned up with Academician

parts.note: to turn up is to arrive, so came
RA is a Royal Academician, member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A photographer arrived with a member of the Royal Academy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' looks like a reversal, but it just means arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that produces photographs, so it makes pictures.

clue.text: Put fizz into cabaret with no cast

indicators.note: cast means thrown, so the letters of cabaret and no are scattered anew

explanation.surface: Livening up a cabaret that has no performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the performers but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge a drink with carbon dioxide makes it fizzy.

clue.text: Catch sight of in wife's pyjamas

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit within the words wife's pyjamas

explanation.surface: Spotting someone in his wife's nightwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot or glimpse something, which is catching sight of it.

clue.text: Drop live commercial

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A broadcaster pulls a live advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rounded drop of liquid, as with a bead of sweat.

clue.text: Ancient poet seen back in Vladivostok

indicators.note: back means the letters found are read in reverse
in shows the letters sit inside the word Vladivostok

explanation.surface: A classical poet was spotted returning to Vladivostok.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman poet of the Metamorphoses, so an ancient poet.

clue.text: Make weak argument about Lilith going naked

indicators.note: about means the argument word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a debate is an argument

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer letters, so Lilith loses its ends

explanation.surface: A feeble dispute over Lilith appearing nude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going naked' strips Lilith of its outer letters, and 'about' wraps the argument around them; Lilith is Adam's first wife in Jewish folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap strength or enfeeble, a synonym of making weak.

clue.text: Only crack when victor departs

indicators.note: departs means the victor letter leaves the word for crack

parts.note: to crack a puzzle is to solve it
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A crack appears only once the winner leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Single and sole are synonyms of only, as in the sole survivor.

clue.text: Berkshire town's first leader

parts.note: a maiden voyage or speech is a first
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: A Berkshire town's original mayor.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkshire is an English county west of London; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidenhead is a town on the Thames in Berkshire, England.
